patients.summary: Retired construction foreman and heavy smoker with hypertension, type 2 diabetes on basal insulin, chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin and CKD 3a, managed by the practice from 2022. A 2025 hernia repair records a look-alike vial near miss; in 2026 a warfarin-associated left intracerebral hemorrhage with cocaine-induced vasculopathy, then a massive PE complicated by bleeding on heparin. Outside records are sparse.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Dupuis phoned wanting to transfer his primary care here; his longtime doctor is retiring. Retired, insured, lives in Granby. Says he is on a blood thinner that needs regular finger-stick checks and wants to know if we can do those in the office. Told him yes, our nurses run INR checks. Booked new patient visit 9/13 at 8:40. Release of records form emailed for his prior practice. Asked him to bring all pill bottles and his insulin pen to the visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o retired construction foreman transferring care; his prior internist is retiring. Brought every bottle plus his glargine pen.

Active issues he brings:
- Hypertension, years, on amlodipine 5 and metoprolol tartrate 50 BID. No home cuff.
- Type 2 diabetes on glargine 20 units at bedtime. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, mostly 130s-160s by his report. No lows he knows of.
- Atrial fibrillation, chronic, rate controlled on metoprolol, anticoagulated with warfarin 5 mg nightly for as long as he can remember, goal INR 2-3. Prior office did monthly finger sticks. No bleeding, no palpitations he notices.
- CKD stage 3 per his old office; he knows his kidneys are 'a little slow'.

PSH: gallbladder out around age 45. Left femur fracture at about 62, fixed with plate and screws.
FH: father had an MI at 72 and high blood pressure. Mother had diabetes and kidney disease. Brother had a stroke at 70.
SH: married, lives with wife in Granby. Smokes a pack a day, has for about 45 years. A drink or two on weekends. Denies other substances.
Allergies: none to medications.

ROS: no chest pressure, no dyspnea on stairs, no melena, no hematuria, no easy bruising, no foot numbness.

Exam: well appearing, weathered. BP and weight per flowsheet. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs with good air movement, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, old RUQ scar. Healed lateral left thigh scar. Feet: intact skin, monofilament normal both feet, pedal pulses present. No edema.

A/P:
1. Chronic AF on warfarin - we will take over INR monitoring, point-of-care INR today, then every 4 to 6 weeks with the nurse. Reviewed bleeding precautions and that new antibiotics or OTC pain relievers should go past us first.
2. HTN - at goal in the office today, continue current doses.
3. T2DM - A1c, urine albumin/creatinine today. Continue glargine 20 units.
4. CKD 3a - CMP today, avoid NSAIDs.
5. Tobacco - advised quitting in plain terms. He is not interested right now, 'smoked through worse'. Will keep asking. Qualifies for lung cancer screening: low-dose CT ordered after shared decision talk. AAA screening ultrasound ordered as well.
6. Health maintenance - records requested; PCV20 and high-dose flu given today. Hep C antibody once.

Return 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Dupuis, your labs from yesterday are back. INR was in range, so keep the same warfarin dose and see the nurse in about four weeks. A1c is a bit above where I'd like it but close; we'll recheck in December before deciding anything. Kidney function is at the same level your old office described. Hepatitis C test was negative. Call or message with any questions.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records received from patient's previous internist, 38 pages, scanned to media. Summary entered by MA: problem list matches ours (HTN, T2DM on basal insulin, chronic AF on warfarin, CKD 3). Screening colonoscopy 2018, no polyps, repeat in 10 years. Tdap 5/2017. COVID Moderna x2 in Feb/Mar 2021 and booster Nov 2021. INR log from 2021-2022 shows values mostly 2.1-2.9 on 5 mg daily. Abstracted to chart; immunizations entered.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening, current smoker, 45 pack-years. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none. Findings: no pulmonary nodules. Lung parenchyma clear. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Cholecystectomy clips. Visualized upper abdomen otherwise unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: POC INR fingerstick. No missed doses, no bleeding or bruising, no new meds, diet unchanged. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily. Next INR ~5 weeks, scheduled with COVID booster.

reports.text: Limited abdominal aortic ultrasound for AAA screening. The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximal diameters: proximal 2.0 cm, mid 1.9 cm, distal 1.8 cm. No aneurysmal dilatation. Common iliac arteries normal caliber.

documents.title: INR and COVID booster
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR by fingerstick, result reviewed with pt. Warfarin unchanged, 5 mg nightly. Bivalent COVID booster given L arm; observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Reminded of December diabetes visit.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing fine. Fasting sugars he's logged run 140s. Taking glargine every night. Still a pack a day. Snow-blowing without chest symptoms or shortness of breath. No bleeding on warfarin.
O: Vitals per flowsheet. Irregularly irregular, rate fine. Lungs clear. Feet warm, no lesions. No edema.
A/P: T2DM, A1c drawn - will message. Glargine 20 units for now. HTN controlled on amlodipine/metoprolol. AF: INR today, warfarin unchanged. CKD 3a, BMP. Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. Tobacco: asked again, declines help. RTC March.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fingerstick INR. No bleeding, no missed doses, no med changes. Same dose. Recheck 6 weeks.

documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting 90-day supply of glargine pens and pen needles; new plan year changed his Part D preferred brand. Sent new rx for glargine 100 units/mL pens, 20 units at bedtime, 90-day supply, plus pen needles, per standing order. Pharmacy confirmed covered.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Quick check. Feels well. Sugars similar. Arm was sore after the first shingles shot, wants to get the second over with.
Exam: irregular rhythm, controlled rate; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: A1c and INR today. No changes to glargine, warfarin, amlodipine or metoprolol. Shingrix #2 given, series complete. Smoking: precontemplative. Follow up in about 3 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR checked. Denies bleeding. Continue 5 mg nightly. Next check early June.

documents.title: Forgot my warfarin last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I think I missed my coumadin last night, the pill box still has it this morning. Do I take two tonight?

documents.title: RE: Forgot my warfarin last night
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good morning Mr. Dupuis. Please do not double up. Take your usual single 5 mg tablet tonight and carry on as normal. One missed dose is not a problem; your next INR check is already on the books. Call us if you notice any unusual bleeding or bruising.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife called to cancel tomorrow; he has a work commitment he can't move. Rebooked 6/27, INR to be done at that visit.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels well. Busy with odd carpentry. No bleeding or bruising. No chest symptoms with work.
Exam: comfortable. Skin without bruising. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled. Lungs clear. Feet ok.
A/P: AF on warfarin, INR today, dose unchanged; reviewed fall and ladder safety on a blood thinner. T2DM, A1c and BMP drawn. HTN fine. Eye exam due - gave him the optometry list. Smoking unchanged. Next: annual wellness visit in September.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Diabetic eye exam, dilated, 7/20/2023. Patient with type 2 diabetes on insulin. Medications reviewed; no known drug allergies. VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. IOP normal both eyes. Lenses clear. Fundus: no hemorrhages, no microaneurysms, no exudates; maculae flat. Impression: no diabetic retinopathy either eye. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Anticoagulation check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: POC INR. No bleeding, no dietary changes beyond garden greens, which he eats steadily all summer. Continue current dose.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, first here. Lives with his wife, independent with everything, drives, does odd carpentry for friends. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine for conversation. Vision corrected, eye exam July without retinopathy. PHQ-2 negative. Advance directive: wife is his health care proxy, paperwork not done - gave forms.

Chronic conditions reviewed: AF on warfarin with INRs mostly in range; HTN controlled; T2DM on glargine 20 units; CKD 3a stable on prior labs.

Exam: irregularly irregular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses present, skin intact. No edema.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028. Tdap 2017. PCV20 done. Shingrix done. Flu today. Updated COVID shot when it reaches the pharmacy here next month. Lung screening due again in October - order placed. Still smoking a pack a day; advised to quit, offered help, not ready.

Labs today per orders.
